analysis_steps.goal: Measure line fluxes, widths, redshifts and sizes

method.value: Gaussian fit to spectra integrated within the 2 sigma contour; 2D Gaussian fit to intensity maps, deconvolved with beam

evidence.quote: We calculate the line widths, redshift, and fluxes of CO $(8-7)$, $(9-8)$ and $\rm H_{2}O$ by fitting a Gaussian profile to the spectra.

fitting.value: single Gaussian; OH+ center fixed to [CII] redshift

evidence.quote: so we fix the center frequency to the \[C II\]$\rm \ 158\mu m$ redshift

validation.value: Compared to previous CO(6-5) and [CII] measurements

evidence.quote: The new NOEMA observation yield a CO $(6-5)$ flux of 1.05 $\pm$ 0.07 Jy $\rm km \ s^{-1}$, consistent with the results obtained with ALMA

analysis_steps.goal: Fit CO SLED with MOLPOP-CEP slab grid

method.value: Least squares and emcee on grid of uniform slabs (10 zones), one- and two-component models

evidence.quote: we first apply the least square method to find the best fitting results. We also use the Bayesian code emcee

key_parameters.value: X_CO=1e-4, local linewidth 1 km/s, CMB 19.12 K, 10 zones

evidence.quote: we fix the molecular abundance of CO to $X_{\rm CO} = 10^{-4}$ (Milky Way, (cite: blake87)), and local linewidth to 1 $\rm km\ s^{-1}$

assumptions.value: Tkin>19.12 K; N(CO)Phi<3.2e19 cm-2 from dynamical mass; N(CO)/n(H2)<1.1e18 cm

evidence.quote: The fact that $T_{\rm kin}$ is hotter than the background CMB radiation at redshift 6 is a prior, which sets $T_{\rm kin} >$19.12 K.

fitting.value: Cold component fixed at Tkin 50 K, log n 4.2, log N(CO) 18.0 in two-component fit (five free parameters)

evidence.quote: With this assumption, we are fitting only five instead of eight parameters.

validation.value: Results consistent within 1 sigma with/without CO(10-9)

evidence.quote: The resulting parameter ranges are consistent within 1$\sigma$ between including and excluding the CO $(10-9)$ line in the fitting procedure.

findings_qualitative.value: CO SLED peaks at J=8, higher than local starbursts, SMGs and local AGNs

evidence.quote: while the J2310+1855 CO SLED peaks at much higher $J$ transitions at $J=8$

claims.hypothesis: The J>=5 CO emission arises from warm dense gas
claims.experiment: MOLPOP-CEP grid fit with emcee, one and two components
claims.finding: CO SLED dominated by warm dense component

evidence.quote: Either one or two component model suggests that the CO SLED detected within the nuclear region

claims.hypothesis: Excitation is higher than in starbursts
claims.experiment: Compare SLEDs with (U)LIRG, SMG, AGN samples

evidence.quote: The CO SLED of J2310+1855 shows higher excitation compared to local/high redshift starburst samples and local AGNs.

claims.hypothesis: UV from stars alone does not power the gas
claims.experiment: H2O/CO and OH+/H2O ratios versus literature
claims.finding: Shocks, cosmic rays or X-rays likely contribute

evidence.quote: are suggesting other heating and ionization sources (e.g., cosmic rays, shocks and X-rays) in addition to PDR.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: One-component model underpredicts CO(8-7), motivating a two-component model

evidence.quote: But the current best fit model fail to reproduce the very high CO $(8-7)$ line flux detected.

limitations_admitted.value: OH+ detection tentative (4 sigma); data insufficient to constrain all eight two-component parameters

evidence.quote: Our data are insufficient to constrain all eight parameters.

referee_caveats_inferred: Cold component is fixed from another quasar, so the two-component result is assumption-driven
Single-slab models with 1 km/s linewidth are crude
Different beams across lines may bias SLED ratios
